title: Quant-aware KV-eviction and memory profile tuning for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build and validate quantization-aware, model-specific memory profiles and a tiered KV-eviction policy to reduce peak GPU memory for long-context serving (32k+ and 128k configs) across representative Llama, Mistral, and Qwen variants. This ticket covers profiling, profile generation, runtime integration, and staged rollout. Motivation: continuous batching and large KV caches push peak memory beyond available headroom for Dedicated instances; naive eviction or uniform profiles either degrade throughput or increase hallucination risk. Outcome should be a deterministic memory-profile artifact per model+context+quantization that lets the serving runtime calculate safe batch sizes, KV allocation, and eviction thresholds with measurable cost/latency improvements.
acceptance_criteria: Validated memory profiles produced for at least three model variants (one Llama-xx, one Mistral-xx, one Qwen-xx) across two long-context configs (32k, 128k)
Peak GPU memory reduced by >=18% (median across workloads) compared to baseline for long-context synthetic replay workloads, with 95p latency regressions <5%
Automated pipeline commits profile artifacts to model-catalog and exposes metadata used by runtime kernel-selection and batch-scheduler
End-to-end integration tests in staging show no increase in token-level decoding errors attributable to KV-eviction (false positive rate <0.2% on eval prompts)
Runbook and rollout plan written and reviewed by SRE/Runtime owners
plan: Phase 1: Micro-profiling — collect per-layer memory + KV growth traces using instrumented load harness for target models (dynamic batch sizes, seq lengths up to 128k)
Phase 2: Profile synthesis — generate quant-aware profiles that include: static parameter bytes, quant table overhead, peak activation footprint by prefix-length, and KV-reservation guide lines
Phase 3: Runtime integration — add profile lookup to kernel-selection path; implement tiered KV-eviction (prefix-priority, key-age buckets, size-based spill-to-disk simulation for on-prem configs)
Phase 4: Perf validation — run continuous-batching load tests with mixed workloads, capture latency/cost/memory traces, tune eviction thresholds
Phase 5: Staged rollout — enable on staging Dedicated clusters behind feature flag, gather telemetry for one week, then gradual ramp to selected customers
risks: Quantization-aware profiles may under-estimate transient activation peaks for certain operator fusions -> OOMs in edge cases
Aggressive KV eviction could increase context window misses, resulting in degraded token quality or hallucinations
Profiling noise across hardware types (A100 vs H100 vs customer on-prem GPUs) could require per-hardware variants
Complexity in runtime path increases maintenance burden and regression surface
mitigations: Conservative headroom factor (initially 1.12) applied to synthesized profiles; can be reduced after stable runs
Eviction policy includes a 'sticky prefix' whitelist for immediate past tokens used by safety hooks
Collect hardware-tagged traces and auto-generate profile suffixes per GPU family in the catalog
Add CI floor tests that run a subset of long-context traces on PRs touching memory path
steps: Instrument model runtime to emit per-step memory telemetry (Marcus)
Run profiling harness across selected models and quant configs (Aisha)
Build profile generator and validate artifacts in local staging (Marcus)
Implement tiered KV-eviction in runtime with feature flag (ENG runtime team)
Execute perf regression matrix and produce dashboard summary (Perf eng)
Draft rollout runbook and customer communication template (SRE/PM)
Postmortem template ready in case of regressions (on-call)
Merge PRs and enable feature flag behind runtime-1.24 canary
